signed_rows.behavior: The devcontainer image installs ovsync from openviking_extensions pinned to the ov-sync-v0.3.0 tag.
signed_rows.fails_when: the Dockerfile has no uv tool install of ov-sync, or installs it from a branch, another tag or no ref
signed_rows.command: uv run --directory cli pytest tests/test_devcontainer_volumes.py -q -k ovsync_is_installed_at_the_pinned_tag

signed_rows.behavior: devcontainer.json bind-mounts the host's ~/.openviking directory read-only at /home/vscode/.openviking.
signed_rows.fails_when: no mount has source ${localEnv:HOME}/.openviking, target /home/vscode/.openviking, type bind and readonly, or the mount names the ovcli.conf file instead of the directory
signed_rows.command: uv run --directory cli pytest tests/test_devcontainer_volumes.py -q -k openviking_credentials_are_read_only

signed_rows.behavior: The ~/.ovx bind mount stays writable, so ovx -L can store a token from inside the container.
signed_rows.fails_when: the ~/.ovx mount is gone or carries readonly
signed_rows.command: uv run --directory cli pytest tests/test_devcontainer_volumes.py -q -k ovx_stays_writable

signed_rows.behavior: A how-to in docs/how-to tells the reader to create ~/.openviking on the host with ovx --bind localstack and ov language en before building the container, to refresh the token on the host, and to log in inside the container only with ovx -L --no-bind; it passes the how-to skeleton test.
signed_rows.fails_when: no docs/how-to page names all of ov language en, --bind localstack and ovx -L --no-bind, or uv run --directory cli pytest tests/test_how_to_skeleton.py fails
signed_rows.command: grep -l 'ov language en' docs/how-to/*.md | xargs grep -l -- '--bind localstack' | xargs grep -l -- 'ovx -L --no-bind' | grep -q . && uv run --directory cli pytest tests/test_how_to_skeleton.py -q

signed_rows.behavior: After a rebuild on the operator's host, ovsync --help runs, touch ~/.openviking/x fails with a read-only error, and ovsync reaches the lab OpenViking with the host's credentials.
signed_rows.fails_when: any of the three fails in the rebuilt container; judged after the operator rebuilds, since the build cannot rebuild its own container
